entries.what_happened: One manuscript, 'The hypercube Ramsey number has linear order' (OpenAI, dated 23 September 2026). Its main theorem (Theorem 1.1 in build/sections/01-introduction.tex, repeated in the abstract) claims that there is an absolute constant C > 0 with R(Qₙ) ≤ C·2ⁿ for every integer n ≥ 0. Here Qₙ is the n-dimensional cube graph, and R(H) is the least M such that every red-blue colouring of the edges of K_M contains a monochromatic copy of H, not required to be induced. The abstract says this resolves the Burr–Erdős hypercube Ramsey conjecture positively. The introduction also gives the lower bound R(Qₙ) ≥ 3·2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, from an explicit two-block colouring, so R(Qₙ) is of order 2ⁿ. Two corollaries are stated: for a spanning subgraph F of Qd, R(F^□k) ≤ C·|V(F)|ᵏ with the same C for all k; and for a subgraph H of Qd with 2ᵈ ≤ A·|V(H)|, R(H) ≤ C·A·|V(H)|. The method is a proof by contradiction along sequences, with a discrepancy and patch-tiling argument over eighteen sections, ending in a Hall-matching step.
entries.delivers: Only under a graph-Ramsey reading of 'the Ramsey numbers' (the scope note allows Ramsey numbers of graphs H). On that reading, the claim fixes the order of growth of the two-colour cube Ramsey numbers: linear in the number of cube vertices, with an unspecified constant. The manuscript does not say it settles this problem, and its statement is not the list's: it concerns cube graphs, not classical numbers R(r,s). On the classical reading (R(r,s) for pairs r, s, and in particular R(5,5)), the manuscript gives no value or bound for any R(r,s), does not discuss R(k,k), and uses 'diagonal' only to mean that the cube grows in both colours. It delivers nothing for that reading.
entries.remains: On the graph-Ramsey reading: the constant C is not identified, and the paper says it does not determine whether R(Qₙ)/2ⁿ converges or what its limit would be. On the classical reading, everything in problem_asks remains open: R(r,s) for all pairs r, s, and the exact value of R(5,5), which problem_asks records as known only to satisfy 43 ≤ R(5,5) ≤ 46. The manuscript does not touch R(5,5).
entries.direction: proves the Burr–Erdős hypercube conjecture positively (linear order, unspecified constant); no bearing on classical R(r,s) or R(5,5)
entries.object: No explicit upper-bound object. The upper bound is proved by contradiction and gives no colouring of K_{C·2ⁿ} and no numerical C. The explicit object is the two-block lower-bound colouring for n ≥ 1: vertex blocks of sizes 2ⁿ − 1 and 2ⁿ⁻¹ − 1, edges inside a block red, edges between the blocks blue. A red Qₙ does not fit in a block, and a blue Qₙ would need 2ⁿ⁻¹ vertices in each block. The text attributes this construction to Conlon, Fox, Lee and Sudakov.
entries.doubts: The text flags no step as unproven, and the abstract and Theorem 1.1 agree. Points in the text that bear on how far to read it at face value: (i) the argument is non-constructive and gives no numerical C; (ii) the proof is long, roughly 10,000 lines of TeX across eighteen sections and an appendix table of regimes, and it works with constants chosen in a stated order and 'for large n' conventions throughout; (iii) build/sections/02-reduction-and-notation.tex (lines 59–60) says: 'We leave integer roundoffs in scales and layer counts implicit when the accompanying asymptotic inequalities have slack'; (iv) the late-prefix transfer lemma (build/sections/18-late-dynamics-and-its-transfer-problem.tex, Lemma late-prefix-transfer), which the text itself names as the step still needing a transfer, is given after a short roadmap and then as compressed estimates.
